candidates: When a PR adds or modifies only CI/infrastructure files (e.g. GitHub Actions workflow files, configuration, scripts) without changing any released package's source or public API, flag any included changeset for removal. In this project, changesets are reserved for changes that require a package release (features or bug fixes); pure tooling or workflow changes should not generate a changeset.

When reviewing GitHub Actions workflow `on.pull_request.paths` triggers, verify that every path pattern directly corresponds to a file or file type that the workflow actually validates or depends on. Flag and remove speculative or tangential path selectors (e.g. `**/*.js` on a workflow that only validates a lockfile) — unnecessary triggers cause the workflow to run on unrelated PRs and obscure the workflow's intended scope.

Validation failure messages in CI workflows must be specific and actionable: each message should (a) clearly identify what problem was detected and (b) include the exact remediation steps or commands needed to fix it. A message that names the violation without providing a fix forces developers to investigate the solution independently and slows down the correction cycle.
